tasks.title: The Theory of Continental Drift
paras: Continental drift refers to the idea that the present continents once formed a single， giant continent called Pangaea, and since that time have been slowly drifting apart. In 1915 the originator of this idea, the German meteorologist Alfred Wegener, was impressed by the close resemblance of coastlines of continents on opposite sides of the Atlantic Ocean, particularly South America and Africa. However, the configuration of the coastlines results from erosional and depositional processes and therefore is constantly being modified, so even if Wegener was right and the continents had separated in the distant past, it is not likely that the coastlines would fit exactly. But decades later it was shown that the continents fit together well along the continental slope (the broad underwater shelf on the edges of continents), where corrosion is minimal, and recent studies have confirmed the close fit between continents when they are reassembled to form Pangaea.

If the continents were at one time joined, then the rocks and mountain ranges of the same age in adjoining locations on the opposite continents should closely match. Such is the case for the continents thought to have together formed the southern supercontinent Gondwana when Pangaea broke up into a northern and a southern supercontinent, mostly during the Jurassic period (200-146 million years ago). Antarctica, South America, Africa, Australia-New Guinea, and India comprised Gondwana. Marine, nonmarine, and glacial rock sequences of the Pennsylvanian epoch (325-299 million years ago) to the Jurassic period are almost identical for all five Gondwana continents, strongly indicating that they were joined at one time. The trends of several major mountain ranges also support the hypothesis of continental drift.

questions.stem: What does the passage mainly discuss?

options.A: Evidence supporting the theory of continental drift
options.D: Jurassic period rock formations in Gondwan

questions.analysis: 题型：主旨题 原文定位: 全文首句提出大陆漂移理论（Continental drift refers to...） 第一段：海岸线/大陆坡的吻合证据 第二段：岩石序列与山脉走向的匹配证据 选项分析: 全文围绕支持大陆漂移学说的证据链展开： ① 海岸线与大陆坡的拼合性 → ② 冈瓦纳大陆的相同岩石序列 → ③ 山脉走向一致性。 选项(B)仅提及魏格纳背景，(C)(D)为局部细节。

questions.stem: Why do the continents fit together more closely at their continental slopes than at their coastlines?

options.A: The continental slopes were once located above water.
options.B: The continental slopes have experienced much less erosion than the coastlines.
options.C: The continental slopes have experienced less drift than the coastlines.
options.D: The continents were joined only at their continental slopes when they formed Pangaea.

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文定位: 第一段中部 "the continents fit together well along the continental slope... where corrosion is minimal" 选项分析: 原文明确大陆坡因侵蚀作用最小（corrosion minimal）而保留原始形状，海岸线则因侵蚀/沉积作用（erosional and depositional processes）不断变形。选项(D)错误，大陆并非仅在坡相连。

questions.stem: The word "adjoining" in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: 题型：词汇题 原文定位: 第二段首句 "rocks and mountain ranges... in adjoining locations on opposite continents" 选项分析: "adjoining" 指地理上相邻的位置（如非洲与南美边缘），(B) "bordering"（接壤的）最贴合。 干扰项：(A) "similar"（相似）忽略空间关系；(D) "coastal"（沿海的）缩小范围。

questions.stem: How do rock sequences help to provide evidence for the theory of continental drift?

options.A: The rock sequences of the Gondwana continents begin to differ in the Pennsylvanian epoch when the continents started to break up.
options.B: The glacial rock sequences of the Gondwana continents are more similar to each other than they are to either marine or nonmarine rock sequences.
options.C: Rock sequences are nearly the same across the five Gondwana continents from the Pennsylvanian epoch to the Jurassic period.
options.D: Glacial rock sequences are nearly identical in North America, Ireland, Great Britain, and Norway.

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文定位: 第二段中部 "Marine, nonmarine, and glacial rock sequences... almost identical for all five Gondwana continents" 选项分析: 跨大陆的相同岩石序列（宾夕法尼亚纪至侏罗纪）证明大陆曾相连。选项(A)错误：岩石差异始于分裂后（非宾夕法尼亚纪）；(B)(D)偏离冈瓦纳核心证据。

questions.stem: Why does the author mention "the trends of several major mountain ranges" at the end of the second paragraph?

options.A: To contrast mountain formation processes in Gondwana with those in other continents
options.B: To question the accuracy of dating methods for ancient rock sequences
options.C: To emphasize that geological features align when continents are reconstructed as Pangaea
options.D: To suggest that mountain ranges are unrelated to continental drift

questions.analysis: 题型：修辞目的题 原文定位: 第二段结尾 "The trends of several major mountain ranges also support the hypothesis..." 选项分析: 写作逻辑链: ① 提出假设（大陆相连则地质特征应匹配）→ ② 岩石证据 → ③ 山脉走向作为补充证据。 功能：证明大陆重组后地质特征（岩石+山脉）的吻合性。
